meta.title: Expanding FreshCart's private-label range
meta.subtitle: Discussion document for the CEO
meta.purpose: Decide whether to expand the private-label range
meta.confidentiality: Fictional company; numbers from provided research

inputs.label: User-provided research on FreshCart private label
inputs.content:
- Private label is 18% of our sales vs. 26% for the US grocery average (2025).
- Private-label gross margin is 38% vs. 29% for national brands in our stores.
- Our private-label sales grew 9% a year 2022–25; national brands grew 2%.
- Shopper survey (n=1,200, 2025): 64% would buy more private label if quality matched; 41% say our private label is 'hard to find' in store.
- Category gaps: we have no private label in snacks (7% of sales) and frozen (9% of sales); dairy private-label share is 31%.
- Two peers that pushed private label to 30% of sales took 4–5 years and invested about $40M each in product development and packaging.
- Supplier capacity: our current co-manufacturers can add about 1.5 points of private-label share per year.

storyline.governing_thought: FreshCart should raise private label to the US average of 26% within about five years, through entry into snacks and frozen, improvement in product quality and shelf visibility, and new supplier capacity

exec_summary.text: Private label is our most profitable, fastest-growing range, and closing its gap to the US average would lift gross margin by about 0.7 percentage points

sub_points.text: Private label makes up 18% of our sales, against a US grocery average of 26%
Its gross margin is 9 percentage points above national brands (38% compared with 29%), and its sales grew 4.5 times as fast in 2022–25
Moving 8% of sales from national brands to private label at today's margins adds about 0.7 percentage points of gross margin

exec_summary.text: Shoppers want more private label, and snacks and frozen offer the most room because we sell none there

sub_points.text: 64% of shoppers would buy more private label if its quality matched national brands, and 41% say it is hard to find in store
We sell no private label in snacks and frozen, which together make up 16% of our sales
In dairy, where we do offer it, private label already holds 31% of category sales

exec_summary.text: Peers needed years and about $40M each, and our current suppliers set a slow pace, so we should start four moves now

sub_points.text: Two peers took 4–5 years and invested about $40M each to raise private label to 30% of sales
With current co-manufacturers alone, our private label reaches the US average only in 2031
Four moves: entry into snacks and frozen, better product quality, more visible shelf presence and new co-manufacturers

next_steps.action: Build the snacks and frozen range plan and quality benchmarks vs. national brands
Run a shelf-visibility pilot (placement, signage, packaging) in a set of stores
Source and qualify new co-manufacturers for snacks and frozen
Approve a five-year program budget and share targets
